# SEEN-008 is merged without a delivery receipt, by decision

Recorded before the merge, so the journal carries the decision rather than its consequence.

## What was waived

`needs_two_reviewers` is true for this ticket. Measured rather than recalled:
`full_depth_rules` returns `['billing', 'migration']`, `billing` is in `REVIEWED_TWICE`, and
`_implementer_tools` is `{'claude'}`. The last requirement of the review gate is `named - worked_by`
being non-empty, where `named` is the tool prefixes of `reviewer` and `second_reviewer` intersected
with `[actors] assistants`, which is `['claude', 'codex']`. Six reviews read this tree and every one
was a Claude Code subagent, so `named` is `{'claude'}` and the difference is empty. The gate refuses,
correctly, and no value typed into the record would change that without being a falsification.

So there is no `review` record, no `advance` out of review, no `verify-delivery` and no receipt hash.
`verify-merge` has nothing to check the merge against. The ticket's frontmatter stays at `review`,
because `done` is what a receipt earns.

## Why, and who decided

Three Codex rounds before these six each died on a usage limit. Ruud was given three options with the
position stated: wait for Codex and get a real receipt, narrow `REVIEWED_TWICE` as its own harness
ticket, or merge without one. Ruud chose the third and said so explicitly. The recommendation on
record was the first if a day could be spared and the third only on Ruud's word, which is what
happened.

## What the merge is resting on instead

Six full-depth reviews, 22 findings from F67 to F88, every one resolved. The last two reviews broke
nothing of the schema kind: all five acceptance criteria measured by execution against the live
database rather than read out of this journal, tenancy over both relation families at 29 of 29 on
three questions, the cross-tenant read measured with a claim, with no claim and with a malformed
claim, the criterion-4 indexes measured unique and non-partial, the seed compared cell by cell with
the routing table. Regression 311 green at 1,436 tests and 63 subtests. Coverage flat at its
baseline, with F26 standing against the harness about what that figure measures.

## What it costs, stated rather than softened

Both highs of this stretch were found by a review and by nothing else: F67, where an evidence row
could name a path no object stood at so an erasure walked past the bytes, and F78, where one update
moved a seller account's credential pointer into another tenant with no audit event written by either
party. `REVIEWED_TWICE` exists to make a second pair of eyes mandatory where a missed defect costs
money, and that is the control being waived on the ticket that produced those two. A seventh reader
might have found a third.

Two limits of the verification are declared in the Outcome and are the honest residue: the suite
measures that the schema refuses an update of a derived member, not that part 9's trigger is what
refuses it, because 17 of 29 tenancy members are refused 23503 by a parent key either way; and
`seen.guard_authored_identifiers()` runs at apply time only, so a later migration adding a table with
a `tenant_id` gets no immutability trigger and nothing hands that obligation forward. The second is
worth a ticket.
